Gold.note: Central bank accumulation and geopolitical hedging sustain premium valuations.

Silver.note: Structural deficits and robust photovoltaic demand drive industrial and monetary upside.

Copper.note: Grid modernization and electrification outpace constrained mine supply growth.

Uranium.note: Structural primary supply deficits coincide with global nuclear capacity expansions.

Lithium.note: Near-term oversupply from new capacity offsets moderating EV demand growth.

Nickel.note: Surging Indonesian supply growth outpaces Class 1 battery and alloy demand.

Zinc.note: Tight concentrate markets and regional smelter production cuts support prices.

Iron Ore.note: Structural weakness in Chinese property development offsets infrastructure stimulus.

Coal.note: Long-term thermal demand destruction limits price upside despite near-term resilience.

Rare Earths.note: Geopolitical export controls and structural EV motor demand tighten supply.

Manganese.note: Steady steelmaking demand balances the market amid nascent battery applications.

PGM.note: South African supply constraints and emerging hydrogen economy potential support prices.

Potash.note: Geopolitical supply disruptions and steady global agricultural fertilizer demand.

Aluminum.note: Chinese production capacity caps and strong green energy demand tighten the market.

Diversified.note: Balanced exposure to both green transition metals and traditional bulk commodities.
